messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: (SEV2) latency SLO routing oscillation detected for service `api-generate` — p95 > 600ms triggers. Triggering rule: latency-based dynamic reroute. Started 2025-11-04T18:42:12Z. Paging oncall-sre.

oncall-sre: Acknowledged, paging routing/runtime. I'll grab paging duty.

Maya (SRE): Oncall here, looking at metrics now. p95 ~1200ms for region-eu-west-1 for the last 8m. Reroute events spiking: ~230 reroutes in last 10m.

Alex (Runtime): Seeing repeated fallback between model variants `gpt-neo-v1-quant` and `gpt-neo-v1-fp` on the same customer keys. KV cache churn looks high.

Jordan (Routing): Policy config looks like this (from control plane):
```json
{
  "policy": "latency_reroute",
  "trigger_p95_ms": 600,
  "window_seconds": 60,
  "cooldown_seconds": 15,
  "max_reroutes_per_minute": 10,
  "fallback_variants": ["gpt-neo-v1-quant","gpt-neo-v1-fp"]
}
```
This cooldown is way too short given backend spin-up and cache effects -> thrash.

Katie (Support): We're seeing customer reports: 3 paid customers in EU experiencing timeouts and degraded responses. One has backing SLA escalation incoming.

Maya (SRE): Quick customer impact estimate: ~0.8% of global requests, but concentrated in eu-west-1 and affecting high-latency tails. Error rate (5xx) up from 0.2% to 1.5%.

Jordan (Routing): Immediate mitigations proposal (short run):
1) Turn off `latency_reroute` for `api-generate` (stop automatic reroutes)
2) Pin traffic for affected customers to `gpt-neo-v1-fp` (stable)
3) Increase cooldown to 120s and add exponential backoff for future policy changes
4) Postmortem and follow-up tuning

Alex (Runtime): Agree. Pinning will avoid cache invalidation churn. I can push a pin to control plane. Suggest we also enable prefix caching sticky behavior for pinned sessions.

Maya (SRE): Execute plan 1+2 now. Jordan/Alex, please coordinate. I'm going to mute alert noise after we have confirmation.

Alex (Runtime): Running control plane call to pin variant for customer group `cust-eu-high`:
```bash
curl -X POST "https://control.redwood.internal/v1/routes/api-generate/pin" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CTRL_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"selector": "cust-eu-high","variant": "gpt-neo-v1-fp","reason": "mitigate reroute thrash"}'
```

Alex (Runtime): API returned 200. Response: `{\"status\":\"ok\",\"applied\":true}`. Pinned ~12% of traffic for eu-west-1 customers.

OpsBot: config-change: route pin applied by Alex (Runtime) at 2025-11-04T18:49:10Z — ticket #INC-2431 created.

Maya (SRE): Now disabling automatic latency-based reroutes for `api-generate`:
```bash
# disable dynamic reroute
curl -X PATCH "https://control.redwood.internal/v1/policies/latency_reroute" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CTRL_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"enabled": false, "reason": "active mitigation - prevent oscillation"}'
```

Maya (SRE): Command returned 200, policy disabled.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Policy `latency_reroute` disabled for `api-generate` by Maya (SRE).

Jordan (Routing): I'm updating the policy draft to safer defaults for later rollout: trigger_p95_ms=800, window_seconds=120, cooldown_seconds=180, max_reroutes_per_minute=2, exponential_backoff=true. Will attach to INC-2431.

Alex (Runtime): Monitoring metrics... p95 in eu-west-1 dropping — 10m window now shows ~620ms -> 560ms as pins take effect. Reroute rate down to ~1-2/min.

Katie (Support): Notified the three customers with an interim note: "We've applied a mitigation to stabilize routing and reduce high latency. We'll follow up with root cause and timeline for permanent fix."

Maya (SRE): Good. I'm going to hand this to Maya (followup owner) — sorry, hand to myself: I'll own post-incident work. Alex/Jordan please keep me posted on policy proposal and runtime observations.

Jordan (Routing): Will push policy draft to staging with tests for cache-churn simulation before re-enabling.

Alex (Runtime): Observability notes for postmortem: look at KV cache eviction rate, prefix cache hit ratio, correlation of reroute events with cold-start latency for `gpt-neo-v1-fp` vs quant. Also check model loading times on eu-west-1 GPU pool.

Maya (SRE): Quick check-in numbers 10m after mitigation:
- p95 eu-west-1: 560ms (was 1200ms)
- reroutes/min: ~1.4 (was 23+)
- 5xx rate: 0.45% (was 1.5%)
- impacted customers flagged: 3 -> all notified

Katie (Support): Customer #C-1290 acknowledged the note and dropped escalation for now.

OpsBot: auto-note: incident state -> mitigated. Incident severity remains SEV2 while follow-up tasks open: INC-2431 (routing policy), PB-857 (runtime cache tuning).

Maya (SRE): Handoff: I'll own follow-up. Jordan/Alex please add your action items to INC-2431. Support, please keep customer comms warm and inform if anything new.

Jordan (Routing): Action items I'm adding:
- run simulation to validate cooldown 180s w/ exponential backoff
- add guard on reroute rate per customer key
- add metric for cache churn correlated to reroutes

Alex (Runtime): My items:
- instrument model load times in eu-west GPU pool (detail traces)
- implement sticky prefix cache for pinned sessions
- verify quantized variant warmup behavior (cold start penalty)

Maya (SRE): Closing notes: No customer data exposure. Root hypothesis: aggressive latency-triggered reroute policy threshold + short cooldown caused rapid oscillation between variants, which amplified tail latency via cache invalidation and cold-starts. Temporary mitigations: policy disabled + targeted pinning. Permanent fix: tuned policy + runtime mitigations and canary in staging.

Maya (SRE): Handoff to daytime ops. I'll draft postmortem and schedule follow-up with Routing/Runtime next week.

Alex (Runtime): Thanks — will follow up in INC-2431 with data dumps.

Katie (Support): Thanks team. I'll update customers after the postmortem.

Maya (SRE): Incident marked mitigated at 2025-11-04T18:53:45Z. Last status update 18:58:45Z.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident INC-2431 mitigated; follow-ups required.

OpsBot: reminder: create postmortem doc and link to INC-2431 within 48h.

Maya (SRE): Signing off the channel, leaving follow-ups to the action owners.
